_meta.fixtures: All 3 cases are fully self-contained synthetic fixtures built inline via `set obs`/`gen`/`replace` — no dependency on the soccer corpus or any external file (per task instructions, synthetic-and-exact preferred over a Stata oracle where the true value is derivable first-principles).

mp1_merge_highprecision_key.bug_citation: piet/native/src/handlers_data_verbs.cpp:2010 (findDupKey) — composite dup-key built via `keyOss << "n:" << v` with default ostream precision (6 significant digits). game_id-class f64 keys that agree on their first 6 significant digits collide in the `seen` map even though they are genuinely distinct, producing a false 'dataset is not unique' merge error. Fix tracked as MI-236 (findDupKey should use eval::pythonFloatRepr, mirroring joinbyRowKeys in the same file).
mp1_merge_highprecision_key.fixture_design: using-side key set deliberately collides at 6 sig figs under two independent classes: (a) 7-digit integers 1005938 vs 1005942 (both format to the identical '1.00594e+06' under default ostream precision — verified live against the baseline, the false-error message cites exactly 'id=1005942.0'); (b) a fractional pair 3141.59261 vs 3141.59264 (both format to the identical '3141.59'). All 4 keys are genuinely UNIQUE on the using side (this is what makes the merge error FALSE). The master side repeats each of the 4 keys exactly twice (m:1 shape, 8 master rows total) so a correct merge must attach the right using-side payout to every master row — not just avoid erroring.
mp1_merge_highprecision_key.using_placeholder_note: Substituted by the driver at run time with a fresh tempdir path (`save`/`use` both need a real filesystem path; the golden JSON itself stays environment-independent).
mp1_merge_highprecision_key.match_atol_rationale: id/payout are literal, untransformed inputs carried through a pure lookup-join (no arithmetic) — a correct engine reproduces them bit-exact. 1e-6 is pure JSON float round-trip safety margin, not a real tolerance budget.

mp2_collapse_factorby_precision.bug_citation: piet/native/src/handlers_data_verbs.cpp:771 (pre-convert CSV write) and :1001 (post-collapse restore CSV write) — both write f64 cell values via `csv << v` (default ostream precision, 6 significant digits) whenever ANY by()-var is a factor (string) column, forcing the whole dataset through a CSV round-trip. The COMPUTED STATISTIC itself (not just the by-var proxy code) is written at line 1001 and silently truncated. A numeric-only by() rides cobra's native fast path and never touches this code — which is why the existing collapse goldens (numeric-by only) missed this class entirely.
mp2_collapse_factorby_precision.fixture_design: 2 groups (string by-var `grp`, forcing the buggy CSV-shim path), 2 obs/group. Every input value is k + m/1024 (dyadic rational, exactly representable in float64 with room to spare in the 52-bit mantissa) so the TRUE mean is representable with ZERO floating-point rounding error — no Stata run needed, the oracle is exact arithmetic. Verified live: mean_alpha*2048 and mean_beta*2048 are both exact integers (2048004 and 4096014 respectively), confirming dyadic exactness.
mp2_collapse_factorby_precision.true_value_derivation: alpha: (1000 + 1/1024 + 1000 + 3/1024) / 2 = 1000 + 2/1024 = 1000.001953125 (13 significant digits). beta: (2000 + 5/1024 + 2000 + 9/1024) / 2 = 2000 + 7/1024 = 2000.0068359375 (14 significant digits). Both exact in binary float64 (first-principles, not display-rounded).

tolerance_policy.rationale: Ratified per MSG-MI-237 item 2's own suggestion. The bug truncates to EXACTLY 6 significant digits, i.e. a relative error of order 1e-6 to 1e-7 on these magnitudes (empirically observed on the baseline: alpha true=1000.001953125 vs got=1000.0 -> rel err ~1.95e-6; beta true=2000.0068359375 vs got=2000.01 -> rel err ~1.58e-6) — 1e-9 sits >1000x below the smallest observed miss, comfortable margin against false-RED on a correct engine (whose only error source is double rounding, ~1e-16) while still >1000x tighter than the bug's signature.

mp3_foreach_continue_capture.bug_citation: piet/native/src/loops.cpp runBody() (~line 534-552, used internally by runForeach/runWhile) checks `b.value("type","")=="error"` with NO exemption for a captured error, unlike doexec.cpp's own top-level halt-check (~line 508/537) which correctly skips `captured:true` blocks (BS-127: 'capture-forwarded errors ... are display-only ... must not HALT a running do-file'). Net effect: the FIRST captured, noisily-shown error inside ANY foreach/while iteration's body silently breaks the iteration loop after that iteration, even though the SAME error would not have halted a non-looped top-level do-file. The do-file itself does not halt (doexec.cpp's own check IS captured-aware) — only the loop's internal iteration advancement does, which is what makes this a control-flow bug rather than a halted-script bug: iterations 2..N are silently skipped and everything AFTER the loop still runs, masking the skip.
mp3_foreach_continue_capture.fixture_design: Exact repro shape verified live by the maintainer before dispatch (MSG-MI-237) and independently re-verified here byte-for-byte against the baseline: `failprog` is a user program whose body runs an unconditional error; `foreach v in a b c` calls it via `capture noisily` each iteration. IMPORTANT PROVENANCE NOTE (so this case is never mysterious later): the do-file never loads a dataset, so `error 111` itself never actually dispatches as Stata's `error N` command (that command is not implemented in this build at all — verified: with a dataset loaded, the SAME line instead falls through to an `unsupported_command` block with rc=199). Without a dataset, PIET's own `session.currentHbin()` pre-dispatch guard fires FIRST and returns a `no_data_loaded` block — whose rc, per piet/native/include/piet/eval/errors.h's documented `coarseRc` map (`no_data_loaded -> "111"`), is a STABLE, INTENTIONAL 111, not a coincidence tied to the literal text 'error 111'. This is precisely why the given repro's rc reads as 111 'correctly' even though no `error` command ever actually ran — documented here so a future reader does not go looking for a nonexistent `error N` dispatch path. The bug being gated (loop-breaks-on-captured-error) is completely independent of which specific error code/class fires; this fixture is simply the minimal, dataset-free, already-verified vehicle for it.

mp3_foreach_continue_capture.caution_honored: Per MSG-MI-237's own caution, the inner display string 'inside-failprog' does NOT begin with the word 'in ' (it begins with the single hyphenated token 'inside-failprog') — empirically re-confirmed live to NOT trip the unrelated `in`-range parser bug.
